metadata.title: De digitale geletterdheid van Nederlandse leerlingen in het voortgezet onderwijs

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses ICILS 2023 assessment data for students in the second year of Dutch secondary education, with sampling at the school level (155 selected schools, 46 realized) and random selection of one or two classes per school, plus teacher sampling within schools. Because the response rate for students and teachers was below IEA guidelines, the authors state that all data were weighted by IEA to correct for non-response and attrition, and that analyses followed IEA standards. The report also notes the use of 75 replicate weights and 5 plausible values for the digital literacy skill scores, indicating a complex survey design with replicate-based variance estimation. The manuscript does not provide the exact weight variable names (e.g., W_FSTUWT), but it explicitly confirms correct use of IEA weights for students, teachers, and schools.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The report describes that IEA used 5 plausible values for the skill scores and that analyses were conducted with IEA weights and replicate weights, but it does not document any explicit missing-data strategy for questionnaire items or test responses (e.g., listwise/pairwise deletion, multiple imputation, or other procedures). Given that ICILS includes both test modules and questionnaires, missingness could arise from non-response to items and incomplete module completion; however, the specific handling approach is not reported in the provided text. This is therefore a reporting gap regarding missing-data treatment.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample comprises students in the second year of Dutch secondary education who participated in ICILS 2023 test sessions on digital literacy. Schools were selected by IEA from a list based on DUO data using a stratified design by education level (pro/vmbo only; havo/vwo only; broad offer), excluding internationally oriented schools, very small schools (<5 students in the second year), special secondary education, newcomer schools, and private schools. Within each participating school, one second-year class was randomly selected for participation (two classes on schools with ≥290 students; one school with all 10 classes). Student data were further analyzed only when sufficient participation occurred at the school level (at least 50% of selected students/teachers participated). Additionally, one school had technical issues such that students completed only CIL and Computationeel denken modules and did not fill the questionnaire; questionnaire outcomes are not reported for that subgroup.

data.outcome_summary: This ICILS 2023 report provides descriptive and multilevel regression results for Dutch students in the second year of secondary education (N=1288 students across 46 schools). The two outcomes are Computer- and information literacy and Computational thinking, each summarized on ICILS proficiency scales with reported mean scores of 460 (CIL) and 440 (CT), both around the lower/baseline levels, and with CIL close to the ICILS average while CT is lower than the ICILS average. Multilevel analyses indicate that education track is the dominant predictor of between-class differences (e.g., >80% of between-class variation attributed to education track), while other student background variables (home language, migration background, parental education/occupation) show limited additional explanatory power after controlling for track. ICT self-efficacy is positively associated with both outcomes, and years of ICT experience is associated with Computational thinking. The report is not an ML predictive-modeling study (no ML algorithms or ML performance metrics are reported); it uses IEA weighting and plausible values (5 PVs) with replicate weights, but missing-data handling procedures are not documented in the provided text.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction targets an official assessment framework, user guide, or technical manual without an empirical ML study. Sample sizes, ML algorithms, and predictive findings are intentionally null or empty per schema rules for non-empirical IEA/OECD documentation.
